objective.statement: Make the consensus-bound Bitcoin miner the exercised workload path while preserving strict no-synthetic-work, non-duplicating shared-volume work allocation, and submission-off-by-default invariants.
objective.acceptance_invariant: A real Bitcoin Core template is the only source of mining work; nonce scanning mutates only the 80-byte header hot path; the full block is assembled only after a target hit; configured network identity matches Bitcoin Core's canonical chain name; repeated/concurrent jobs sharing the canonical allocator cannot silently repeat the same work interval; live submit remains independently gated.

observed.subject: repeated one-shot mining job
observed.source: candidate source readback plus repository search
observed.implication: unchanged template can repeat prior search work when no allocator changes job coordinates

preserved_invariants: Bitcoin Core getblocktemplate remains the authoritative work source.
Live submit is disabled unless KEX_ALLOW_LIVE_SUBMIT is explicitly enabled.
Candidate validation remains bound to target, previous block hash, bits, and current tip before submit.
Consensus construction primitives remain independently testable.
Repository write or commit status is not evidence of mining correctness or promotion.
Prior verified evidence is preserved but cannot be rebound to a changed subject revision without replay.
Workers sharing the canonical allocator state must receive disjoint nonce/extranonce coordinates for an exact template.
A failed CI carrier must not be rewritten as a failed source implementation when no source steps executed.
implemented_candidate_changes: Normalize configured network names to Bitcoin Core getblockchaininfo chain names, including mainnet->main and testnet->test.
Prepare payout script, coinbase, transaction Merkle root, target, timestamp, and extranonce once per work item.
Scan only serialized 80-byte headers in the nonce loop.
Assemble the full block only after a header satisfies target.
Add persistent SQLite work allocation keyed by the exact canonical template descriptor.
Use BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction serialization and append-only allocation history for callers sharing the allocator database.
Advance nonce intervals monotonically and roll to the next uint64 extranonce after the uint32 nonce domain is exhausted.
Store extranonce as decimal TEXT so the full unsigned 64-bit allocation domain is representable in SQLite.
Classify explicit KEX_EXTRANONCE/KEX_NONCE_START coordinates as EXPLICIT_OPERATOR_MANAGED rather than silently treating them as automatically disjoint.
Add forced-hit, exhausted-window, sequential allocation, rollover, changed-template, concurrent allocation, and explicit-allocation tests.
Run btc_miner_runtime.py directly in the M08 workflow, retain proof artifacts, and include an unavailable-RPC negative control.

falsifiers.statement: A forced target hit does not assemble exactly one block.
BTC_NETWORK=testnet does not resolve to Bitcoin Core chain=test.
Unavailable Bitcoin Core RPC produces a candidate, submission, or mining success state.
Repeated or concurrent jobs sharing allocator state can reuse the same default extranonce/nonce interval.

required_before_promotion: Execute the exact candidate head compile and existing Bitcoin consensus tests on an available execution carrier.
Execute the exact candidate head miner/work-allocation falsification suite, including restart/concurrency non-overlap tests.
Execute the unavailable-RPC negative control and observe QUIESCED with no candidate or submission.
Observe live Bitcoin Core qualification with initialblockdownload=false, current best block/tip, and a current getblocktemplate in the candidate execution environment.
Keep live submit independently disabled unless a target-valid candidate exists and explicit submission authority is enabled.
Bind candidate subject, environment, test plan, execution receipts, and promotion decision to the same current revision.

next_route.rule: Do not merge, promote, or advance to M09 while mandatory M08 evidence gates remain open.
